In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, release, and transport of urokinases across the intestinal mucosa and into the circulation of human subjects.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oral administration of HMW UK in humans, in a single dose or in multiple doses, induced the transport of HMW UK across the intestinal tract and the stimulation of synthesis and release of UK-type proteins into the plasma, and induced the fibrinolytically active state.

HMW-UK can be absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and can stimulate the synthesis of a new UK-type protein in the liver or vascular endotheium, which is released into the circulation and converted into active HMW-UK by circulating plasmins.

the oral administration of HMW-type UK to normal human subjects induces a fibrinolytic plasma state by stimulation of synthesis and release of UK-type proteins, and by the conversion of native plasminogen to the Lys-plasminoen form, with no significant adverse effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oral administration of HMW-type urokinase to human subjects induces a fibrinolytic plasma state and stimulates the synthesis and release of a 53,000 molecular weight UK-type protein, probably a UK-zymogen, from the liver and/or vascular endothelium.
the oral route is the best way to induce the plasma fibrinolyte state and to treat thromboembolic disorders.
HMW-UK can induce a systemic fibrinolytic effect in normal human subjects and in patients with thromboembolic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oral route is a promising route for the administration of fibrinolytic agents, and that oral administration of HMW-Uk is a promising therapy in patients with thromboembolic disorders.
oral administration of UK to human subjects induces a plasma fibrinolysis state and that UK-type proteins of high specific activity are produced and/or released into the circulation.
oral HMW-UK is effective in stimulating the synthesis of a zymogen of 53, 000 mol wt, which is probably derived from either the liver and/or vascular endothelium and is released into the circulation.
